Note::remove_all¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove_all(std::string_view needle) const

Delete Every Occurrence Of A Literal Substring¶

remove_all(needle) returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every occurrence of the literal string needle deleted from each cell. It is replace with an empty replacement, given its own name because “strip this marker out entirely” is a common enough intent to be worth spelling directly: separators, bracket noise, a repeated tag, a prefix that leaked into the data.

The match is literal — needle is compared byte for byte, with no regex metacharacters and no case folding. Occurrences are removed left to right and non-overlapping: after one match is cut, scanning resumes at the following byte, so remove_all("aa") on "aaaaa" removes two pairs and leaves one a. Bytes around the deletions are not otherwise touched — no whitespace collapsing, no trimming — so removing a mid-string token can leave a double space; chain strip or replace if that matters.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. A cell that does not contain needle is copied through unchanged.

Example 1: Remove A Repeated Word¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"alpha beta beta", "beta only", "none"}).remove_all("beta"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["alpha  ", " only", "none"]

Both betas go from the first cell (leaving two spaces where they were), the leading beta goes from the second, and the third is unchanged.

Example 2: Matches Do Not Overlap¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"aaaaa"}).remove_all("aa");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["a"]

aa is removed at positions 0 and 2; the trailing a has no pair.

Example 3: A Needle That Is Not Present¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"keep me"}).remove_all("zzz"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["keep me"]

Example 4: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({{"a-b-c", "d-e"}}).remove_all("-"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["abc", "de"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::replace: the general form — substitute a replacement instead of deleting.

  • pluss::coden::Note::remove: delete only the first occurrence.

  • Note::strip: remove characters only at the cell boundaries.

  • Note::NlpAccessor::remove_urls: pattern-based removal (URLs) with whitespace cleanup.
